question: How does an OLED television hide the wear on its most-used pixels?
answer: By measuring the wear and driving tired pixels harder. When the set goes to standby, the panel runs a compensation cycle that senses each subpixel's electrical drift and raises its drive to match, so a worn channel logo fades back into its neighbours. The trick spends spare brightness; burn-in shows once that reserve runs out.
move: A repair that borrows from reserve works until the reserve is gone.
source: Handbook of Visual Display Technology, Springer, 2016
reference: Chen, Cranton & Fihn (eds.), Handbook of Visual Display Technology, 2nd edition, Springer, 2016
